A crouching attack that goes under a high attack does so because ITS BODY IS SHORTER FOR THOSE FRAMES. A `low_profiles: true` flag would make the behaviour a property of the crouching move alone, answer exactly the one question its author thought of, need a second rule for which attacks it profiles under, and be wrong the first time two characters' high attacks sat at different heights. A BOX ANSWERS ALL OF IT AT ONCE: which specific attacks pass over, whether an opponent's sweep still catches it, whether a hop-over clears it, and how much of the character is left exposed. The author's constraint was explicit -- 'not every crouching attack would low profile' -- and a file that states a SHAPE never has to claim that it does. The behaviour falls out of the geometry, which is what makes it checkable in a hitbox viewer rather than assertable in prose. SAME MECHANISM SERVES THE HOP-OVER, from the other side: see airborne_from_tick. SCOPE, STATED SO IT IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR MORE: this is ONE box for the WHOLE move, not a per-frame track. The per-frame form is engine.anim.frames[].hurt and Phase 3 owns it. One box per move is what an author can measure today and what the kernel's FighterData can hold; a move whose profile changes shape mid-animation is over-approximated by the box it authors, and if that matters for a particular move the honest thing is to say so in engine.transcription_note rather than to author the tallest frame and call it exact. ASSERTION A15 refuses a malformed or zero-area box. An EMPTY body is total, permanent, unattributed invulnerability, and this schema already has a field for invulnerability -- engine.invuln[] -- that says which attack classes and for how many ticks. Expressing invulnerability by authoring a degenerate rectangle would hide the strongest property a move can have inside four coordinates that look like a typo.

airborne_from_tick.description: NEW IN v3, the second half of field 3. [E] THE TICK THIS MOVE TAKES THE CHARACTER OFF THE GROUND, or null for the overwhelming majority that never do. Same tick base as move.startup -- tick 1 is the first tick of the state -- so a move may go airborne BEFORE its hitbox appears, which is what a hop kick actually does. THIS FIELD IS WHY HOP-OVERS ARE NOT A BOOLEAN EITHER. The author's example is Ryu's f+HK: a grounded attack that becomes airborne mid-animation passes over a low sweep for exactly as long as it is off the floor. That is a consequence of where the body is, not a property anybody declares about the sweep, and it needs no move to name any other move. This tick plus hurtbox_sub is the whole mechanism, for every pair of moves, symmetrically. A `hops_over_lows: true` flag would be wrong the first time two sweeps had different heights. RELATIONSHIP TO THE THREE NEIGHBOURING FIELDS, because they overlap and only one of them is normative for this question. (1) transitions[].kind = on_land says how the state ENDS -- the landing predicate -- and says nothing about when it left. (2) motion_physics.applies_from_tick says when GRAVITY starts integrating, which coincides with going airborne on Kung Fu Girl's knee and is a different fact: it presumes a transcribed motion track. (3) THIS FIELD is the state-type change itself, MUGEN's `StateTypeSet stateType = A` (corpus/kfg/Specials.cns:692-696), and it is the normative answer to 'is the attacker on the floor on tick N'. It is separate from the other two because a designed hop kick has one and needs neither: forcing an author to transcribe a physics block to say one thing about one tick is how a field goes unauthored. Where a move carries more than one of the three they must agree, and nothing checks that they do -- there is no corpus data behind such a check yet, and an assertion nobody has watched fire is not an assertion. MEANINGLESS ON AN `air` MOVE, which was airborne before it began. Authoring it there says nothing new rather than something false, so nothing rejects it. ASSERTION A14 refuses a tick outside the move: a move cannot make you airborne before it starts or after it has ended.

blocked_as.description: [G] ALTERNATIVE SPELLING of move.blocked_as, accepted so that a file authored against this schema's OWN placement rule -- 'everything the prover cannot see lives under an `engine` key' -- still loads. Where both are present the MOVE-LEVEL one wins and this is ignored. Exactly the arrangement move.hit_condition and engine.hit_condition already have, and the precedent for tolerating two spellings rather than breaking a character file is cancel_families / cancel_rules, which v2 declined to unify for the same reason. A NEW FILE AUTHORS THE MOVE-LEVEL SPELLING; this one exists so that a disagreement about placement is a shrug rather than a field that silently does nothing. See x-v3-changes.two_spellings.

hit_condition.description: [E] v1's free-prose form, RETAINED because kung_fu_girl.json ships it on 17 moves and v2 may not invalidate a v1 file. The structured replacement is move.hit_condition at move level; where both exist the structured one is authoritative and this is provenance.

cancel_window_ticks.description: [open, close] tick pair, or the EMPTY ARRAY for a move that has no cancel window at all. The empty case is load-bearing and was caught by validating this schema against its own three characters: the AOF2 thug's moves have no cancel window, and a draft of this schema with minItems:2 rejected the truthful authoring (ADR-001:541-545). A schema that cannot say 'none' forces an author to invent a window.

variant.description: [E] The sub-character this move belongs to, keyed to engine.variants.list[].id. Present in v1 files already (AOF2 uses it on all 10 moves); v2 gives it a character-level index to point at.

characterEngine.description: [E] Character-level engine data. Ignored by json_spec.py.

schema_version.description: CHANGED IN v2 from const 1 to enum [1, 2], which is what lets an untouched v1 file validate against this schema. WIDENED AGAIN IN v3 to [1, 2, 3], for the identical reason and by the identical argument: without it no v2 file could validate against v3 and the superset claim would be false on its most trivial field. A file declaring 1 is a v1 file being read by a v3 reader and is legal; 2 asserts that its authors knew about the nine fields; 3 asserts that they knew about stance precision, block height, priority and typed invincibility -- which is the ONLY thing that distinguishes a file authoring `crouching`, `blocked_as`, `priority` and `invincibility` from one that simply has none of them, and is therefore the first time this key has been worth reading. Note that all five v3 fields are OPTIONAL and four of them have defaults that change nothing, so `schema_version: 3` on a file authoring none of them is a claim about the author rather than about the data -- which is exactly what this key has always been. Nothing keys off it in code; it is a claim the author makes about themselves.

units.description: The D8 quantization contract, stated once per file so both peers agree at load.

sub_units_per_pixel.description: 256, from ARCHITECTURE.md:47. Every v2 field named *_sub is in these units.

meter_units_per_bar.description: 100. 1 unit = 10 MUGEN power (ADR-001:135), the GCD of every power value in the Phase-0 corpus, so the quantization is exact.

quantized_sources.description: The integer originals of every float in the [P] section: reach_px, pushback_px, scaling_permille, decay_table_permille, damage_hundredths. This is what makes ARCHITECTURE D8 checkable -- the engine loads these and the float [P] fields exist only for the prover.

constants.description: Movement, gravity, friction, pushbox, health, meter ceiling. All integer sub-units. Must cite its source lines.

integrity.description: content_hash and schema_hash, both null until Phase 4 fills them. ARCHITECTURE Phase 4 requires the handshake hash the LOADED POD ARRAYS, not this text, so these are advisory identifiers and never the desync check.

cancel_families.description: Named groups so that N homogeneous edges do not repeat the same condition, delay rule, certainty and caveat N times. An edge carrying engine.family inherits all four. Kung Fu Girl's 134 edges reduce to 4 families plus 4 one-offs this way. IN v2 a family may carry a `condition` predicateList, which is how AOF2's 26 identical opponent gates are authored once.

cancel_rules.description: Alternative spelling of cancel_families, keyed engine.rule. Both are accepted; v1 said 'v2 should pick one' and v2 declines to, because kung_fu_man.json ships cancel_rules and kung_fu_girl.json ships cancel_families, and renaming either would break a v1 file for no gain. New files use cancel_families.

derivation_legend.description: [E] The per-field reading order a character's engine.derivation strings follow. STRING OR OBJECT: kung_fu_girl.json ships it as one prose line, and a draft of this schema that required an object rejected that file. Same defect class as the minItems:2 bug ADR-001:541-545 records -- a schema tightened past what its own characters author.

hit_rules.description: Character-level rules gating whether attacks connect at all. IN v2 this is no longer homeless: the per-move structured form is move.hit_condition, and this object stays as the place to say 'the same rule is on all 17 normals' once instead of 17 times, plus the character-level facts behind it -- Kung Fu Girl disables MUGEN's juggle system (corpus/kfg/System.cns:2590-2593 and :7) in order to run its own.

derivation_defaults.description: The per-field reading rules a move claims when its engine.derivation is the string 'see engine.derivation_defaults'.

moves_with_no_outgoing_cancel.description: Assert that a move being a combo ENDER is a fact about the character rather than an omission in the transcription, and cite the line that proves it.

variants.description: NEW IN v2 -- FIELD 9 of 9 (character-level half). [E] ONE .def IS NOT ONE CHARACTER. ADR-001:286-298 is the finding: AOF2 is 'a spawner plus four disjoint sub-characters. The root player has no attacks, is movetype=I, and is made unhittable (corpus/aof2/States.st:1382-1387); its only job is `type = helper, stateno = 1000, ID = 1000, name = Thug` (States.st:5-44). var(0) = random % 4 is rolled once at spawn (States.st:71-73) and never changes, and anim = base + 100*var(0), so the file is four disjoint sub-automata.' The same section names two more shapes this object must eventually carry and which the AOF2 case does not exercise: Kung Fu Man's var(3) 'adds and removes whole MOVES' (nishi and meikyo require var(3)=2 and are absent from the transcription), and its var(5) 'doubles every special into light/strong with different damage and poweradd' with only the light set transcribed (ADR-001:295-298). A mode variable that changes the move LIST is not a per-move field, which is why the index lives here.

selector.description: How the variant is chosen. AOF2's is rolled once at spawn from random % 4 and never changes, which is what makes the sub-automata DISJOINT and the union reading sound.

prover_reading.description: MANDATORY when list has more than one entry. State that the prover sees the UNION of all variants and what that means for the verdict, in the direction language of ADR-001:224-225. Assertion A11.

breakdown.description: Counts by escape_hatch.kind. The gate reading depends entirely on this split: 1 of 59 under D7's own definition, 23 of 59 under 'needed something schema v1 cannot say' (ADR-001:82-93).

known_losses.description: MANDATORY IN SPIRIT. Every projection from source to schema that loses information, with a soundness note saying whether the loss can HIDE an infinite (acceptable, conservative in the wrong direction but honest) or INVENT one (never acceptable).

measured.description: Verdict, timing and configuration counts from an actual `python -m comboprover analyse` run. Must be re-measured, never predicted.

x-v3-changes.summary: Five fields, two relaxations, ZERO narrowings, zero renames. The mandate is not an ADR item this time -- it is a pair of questions the author asked of the data. The first: 'shouldn't it also have crouching as crouching normals are quite important to a 2D fighting game... also blocking should consider high and low blocking?' The second, arriving after fields 1-3 had landed: 'to ensure anti airs properly work we should also probably consider the arc sys works style of priority over aerial attacks... moves specifically toggled as anti airs - will have priority over aerials. certain invincible reversals would have priority over meaty attacks.' The answer to both, checked against the files rather than assumed, was that the character was incomplete in five specific ways, that three of them had never been written down anywhere, and that THE SAME DEFECT PRODUCED ALL FIVE. Fields 1-3 found crouching living in the word `crouch` inside an id and guard height living in a label reading `(low)`. Field 5 found fighter_a's `special_uppercut` labelled `Uppercut (reversal, invincible 1-6)` -- the frame numbers of the strongest property a move can have, in English, in a display string. MatchBuilder.h had already named the defect for buttons in as many words ('move ids like `stand_lp` carry the information only in the English of their spelling'), ADR-006 recorded it for stance, and this is the third instance of one failure mode.

the_five.closes: MUGEN's statetype is S/C/A/L and this enum had three values, so every crouching move in the corpus -- 6 in Kung Fu Girl, 4 in Kung Fu Man -- transcribed as `ground`, and fighter_a's own `crouch_mk` and `stand_mk` declare an IDENTICAL stance. The loss was not merely accepted; ADR-001 section 6.2 lists what was not transcribed and this is not on it.

the schema had NO CONCEPT OF BLOCK HEIGHT: grep v2 for overhead, blockable, guard_height or attack_height and the answer is zero hits, on a schema for a 2D fighting game. An overhead and a low could not be distinguished from a mid, so every attack in every file was implicitly blockable by any block.

low-profiling and hop-overs, AS GEOMETRY. Counted as one field because they are one mechanism seen from two sides: a crouching attack goes under a high attack because its body is shorter, and a grounded attack goes over a low because it is off the floor. Neither is a flag and neither move names the other.

who wins when both attacks would land ON THE SAME TICK. Nothing in the schema could say it and nothing in the kernel could ask: ResolveHits trades unconditionally and says so in a comment naming this field as Phase 3 work. A plain integer, default 0, higher wins outright and EQUAL IS A TRADE -- so the default reproduces today's behaviour exactly and no existing character changes.

the frames on which a move cannot be hit at all, and by what. THE EVIDENCE IS ONE LABEL: fighter_a's `special_uppercut` reads `Uppercut (reversal, invincible 1-6)`. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT WAS AND WAS NOT MISSING, because the honest version is more useful than the dramatic one -- move.engine.invuln[] HAS EXISTED SINCE v2 and that move authors it correctly, from_tick 1 ticks 6, strikes only, with a source string recording that throws are deliberately excluded. What was missing is threefold and measured: (a) engine.invuln is [E], in MUGEN's letters, and NOTHING LOADS IT -- Games/UntitledFighter/Data/include/cse/data/CharacterData.h lists it by name among the fields deliberately not read -- so the only copy of `1-6` a program could reach was the English one; (b) MUGEN's attribute vocabulary has no guard-height axis at all, so `invincible to lows` was never expressible in it; (c) two copies of one fact, one of them prose, is D8's failure mode, and they agree today only because nobody has edited either.

x-v3-changes.why_geometry_and_not_flags: THIS IS THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT THE AUTHOR SET AND IT DECIDES THE SHAPE OF FIELD 3, so it is recorded here rather than left in a comment. 'The hurtbox shape for the crouching attack would determine this -- not every crouching attack would low profile.' A `low_profiles: true` boolean was therefore the WRONG ANSWER and is not what is built. The difference is not stylistic: a flag is a claim, a box is a measurement. A flag answers exactly one question -- does this move duck the thing its author was thinking about -- and needs a second rule for WHICH attacks it ducks, a third for whether the hop kick clears it, and a fourth the day two characters' high attacks sit at different heights. A box answers all four at once, is checkable in a hitbox viewer, and cannot disagree with itself. The same argument applies to the hop-over from the other side: one tick number saying when the attacker leaves the floor lets every low in the game be evaluated against every hop, symmetrically, with no move naming any other move.
x-v3-changes.why_two_mechanisms_and_not_one: READ THIS BEFORE CHANGING EITHER OF FIELDS 4 AND 5, because what was built is a READING of the request rather than a transcription of it, and the next person is owed the fact that it was a choice. THE REQUEST: 'having a priority system that can be toggled depending on attack state might be a good idea. ie: moves specifically toggled as anti airs - will have priority over aerials.' Taken literally that is ONE field: a per-move table of (condition, priority) pairs. WHAT WAS BUILT IS TWO ORTHOGONAL FIELDS -- a plain integer priority with no conditions at all, and a typed invincibility window list -- and the anti-air case falls out of the SECOND one, not the first. AN ANTI-AIR IS NOT A CATEGORY OF MOVE. It is a move that cannot be hit by an airborne attack during its startup, which is one invincibility window and needs no condition, no toggle and no second vocabulary. A reversal is the same field with a wider kind set. FOUR REASONS, IN THE ORDER THEY DECIDED IT. (1) A condition table is a GRAMMAR. Every condition kind added to it is a new thing the kernel must evaluate at the exact instant two hitboxes overlap, and ADR-002 CHOICE B's discipline is a closed enum rather than an expression language wherever the closed form will do. Here it does. (2) THE TWO COMPOSE AND THE TABLE DOES NOT. Invincibility resolves in the DECIDE phase before priority is consulted at all, so 'anti-air beats aerials' and 'this move beats that move' are answered by different fields, neither field knows about the other, and anything added later meets one mechanism at a time. A conditional priority would have to grow a case for every future property. (3) IT IS THE SAME LESSON AS stance AND blocked_as, one revision later. ADR-006 exists because one and a half fields were carrying four ideas; collapsing two mechanisms back into one field the very next revision, knowingly, would be indefensible. (4) The general mechanism is USEFUL WITHOUT the special case: throw invincibility on recovery, a fully invincible super's flash, and a low-profiling move's high-attack immunity are all the same field and none of them is an anti-air. WHAT THIS READING GIVES UP, STATED HONESTLY BECAUSE IT IS NOT NOTHING: a priority that VARIES BY THE KIND OF THE OTHER ATTACK -- 'beats aerials, loses to grounded mediums' -- cannot be written. Note carefully what IS covered, because the gap is narrower than it first looks: 'wins the exchange but is still hittable when not attacking' is an unconditional priority with no invincibility window, and 'cannot be touched by aerials at all' is an invincibility window with no priority. Only the case where the ORDERING ITSELF depends on the opponent's kind is missing. REVERSED IF a character genuinely needs that -- at which point priority becomes a list of (attack_kinds, value) pairs reusing $defs.invincibilityWindow's token enum rather than a second one, and the integer becomes its default entry.
x-v3-changes.overlap_is_a_union: TWO INVINCIBILITY WINDOWS MAY COVER THE SAME TICK. Nothing refuses it, nothing warns about it, and the loader does not rewrite the list -- the meaning is the UNION of every window covering that tick, and this entry records that as a decision rather than an oversight. WHY NOT REFUSE: overlap is CORRECT AUTHORING and the request's own example is an instance of it. 'A reversal invincible 1-6 and then throw-invincible through its recovery' is most naturally written as one window of 1-6 naming everything and one window of 1-40 naming throw, which overlap on six ticks and mean exactly what they appear to mean. A diagnostic that fires on the motivating example is how a diagnostic gets deleted, and this file already carries the receipt for that mistake in A04's scope_correction. WHY THERE IS NO AMBIGUITY TO RESOLVE: union is commutative, associative and idempotent, so no precedence rule is needed and none is defined. The appearance of ambiguity comes from MUGEN's HitBy controller, which is a WHITELIST -- two overlapping whitelists have no order-independent reading -- and $defs.invincibilityWindow has no whitelist form for precisely this reason. WHY THE LOADER DOES NOT MERGE THE WINDOWS INTO DISJOINT ONES: the loaded list is the authored list, because a designer reads the file, and a loader that turned two authored windows into three normalised ones would make the data a program sees stop matching the document a human edits. Merging is the SEMANTICS, not a rewrite. THE SCOPE CHECK THAT MATTERS HERE, and it is the one this group of assertions was most likely to get wrong: A07 requires hits[].tick strictly increasing and A08 requires the same of motion[].tick, so copying that rule one field over looks obviously right. IT DOES NOT TRANSFER. A hit record and a motion keyframe are APPLIED IN SEQUENCE and their result depends on which came last -- that is what those two assertions protect. An invincibility window contributes to a set union and nothing about it depends on order or on disjointness. Requiring sorted, non-overlapping windows would be a rule inherited from two assertions whose reason does not hold here, which is the identical failure A04 was corrected for: a rule authored from the shape of a neighbouring rule instead of from the data it governs.
x-v3-changes.one_spelling_for_the_other_two: move.blocked_as accepts move.engine.blocked_as as an alternative spelling (see two_spellings). move.priority AND move.invincibility DO NOT, AND THE LOADER REFUSES engine.priority AND engine.invincibility BY NAME rather than ignoring them. This is a considered departure from the decision two keys up, not an inconsistency, and the difference is what sits next door. For blocked_as, BOTH placements were defensible -- the schema's own placement rule argued for `engine` and what the field IS argued for move level -- so tolerating both was cheaper than arbitrating, and the failure mode being avoided was a field that validates and silently does nothing. HERE THE ENGINE NAMESPACE IS ALREADY OCCUPIED BY BOTH NAMES. `engine.invuln[]` is a list of frame windows about invulnerability in MUGEN's letters; `engine.reaction.priority` is MUGEN's HitDef priority parameter, authored with a real value by the AOF2 thug. Accepting `engine.invincibility` beside `engine.invuln`, or `engine.priority` beside `engine.reaction.priority`, would put near-identical names at one nesting level meaning different things in different vocabularies -- which is the exact confusion `blocked_as` was NAMED to avoid against `guard` one level up, and repeating it here would undo that reasoning in the same revision that made it. A REFUSAL NAMING THE RIGHT SPELLING costs the author ten seconds; a second accepted spelling costs every future reader a lookup and leaves the file with two places to check. It is an ordinary load error rather than a numbered assertion, on the same footing as `engine is not an object`: it is a misplaced key, not a false statement about a move.

the_one_risk.$comment: NAMED AS A RISK BECAUSE IT IS ONE, AND NOT DRESSED UP. This is the first time any revision has changed a field the prover reads.
the_one_risk.what_changed: move.stance is [P] -- json_spec.py:72 reads it -- and v3 adds two values to its enum. v2's summary says it 'ADDS NO [P] FIELDS AND RENAMES NONE'; widening a value set is neither of those, and it is also not nothing.
the_one_risk.measured_and_therefore_stated_as_fact: (1) The C++ side is provably unaffected. ThirdParty/comboprover/comboprover.hpp contains no stance concept at all -- zero occurrences -- and Games/UntitledFighter/Data/src/ProverAdapter.cpp never passes stance into comboprover::Character; its only use is ProverAdapter.cpp:565, `if (m.stance != Stance::Any) ++stanced`, which feeds a projection loss count. So the in-editor verdict path cannot see this change and cannot move because of it. (2) THE THREE PHASE-0 FIXTURES ARE NOT TOUCHED BY v3 AND KEEP AUTHORING `ground`, so every number ADR-001 measured is unaffected by construction rather than by re-measurement.
the_one_risk.SETTLED, AND THE ANSWER IS THE BAD ONE: MEASURED BY ADR-006 section 5 and recorded here rather than left as this schema's open question. The reference implementation VALIDATES stance against a closed tuple and RAISES: model.py:120-121 is `if self.stance not in (GROUND, AIR, ANY): raise ValueError(...)`. So a v3 file authoring `stance: "crouching"` IS UNLOADABLE by the unmodified reference implementation. NOTE THE PROVENANCE HONESTLY: model.py is outside this repository and was not read from here; the measurement is ADR-006's and this entry cites it rather than claiming it.
the_one_risk.which_of_the_two_predicted_outcomes_that: THE LOUD ONE, which is the half of the prediction that survives. A ValueError from a tool a designer runs is impossible to miss and cannot produce a wrong verdict quietly -- there is no third outcome in which a bad answer is returned. What it is NOT is free: it breaks this schema's central $comment claim that the format 'remains a strict SUPERSET of the prover's native JSON format ... no export step appears', which ADR-001:70-75 established by measurement and treated as a property worth keeping. And it bites hardest where it is least visible: the C++ header is corner-only by construction (comboprover.hpp:15-24), so PYTHON IS THE ONLY MIDSCREEN PATH, and a v3 character authoring a precise stance could not be analysed midscreen at all.
the_one_risk.the_remedy_and_the_interim_rule: ADR-006 section 5 recommends widening model.py:120's tuple to five values: one line, and provably verdict-neutral because no decision procedure in the reference reads the field -- the same measurement this entry records for the C++ side. The superset claim then narrows honestly to 'superset modulo a one-line enum widening that provably cannot move a verdict', which is a sentence with a measurement behind it rather than a claim that quietly stopped being true. UNTIL THAT LANDS, THE INTERIM RULE IS ALREADY WHAT THIS SCHEMA REQUIRES FOR AN UNRELATED REASON: the three Phase-0 fixtures keep authoring `ground`, because re-transcribing ten moves in three third-party files is a Phase 3 data job. So nothing is blocked except authoring the first `crouching` move in a character somebody wants a MIDSCREEN verdict on. THREE OF THE FOUR ADDITIONS COST NOTHING EITHER WAY: json_spec.py:72 is a bare str() that validates nothing, and blocked_as, engine.hurtbox_sub and engine.airborne_from_tick are invisible to a loader whose _move() reads thirteen named keys and enumerates none -- the identical argument v2 made for hit_condition.
the_one_risk.why_the_widening_still_ships: Because the alternatives are worse and ADR-006 section 5 rejects them on the record. Putting the precise values under `engine` and leaving [P] stance at three preserves the superset exactly and REINTRODUCES THE SPLIT THIS REVISION EXISTS TO CLOSE, with the attacker's state in two places at two nesting levels. Authoring both -- `ground` for the prover, a precise value elsewhere -- is that option with the redundancy made explicit and two things to keep in sync by hand, which is D8's failure mode wearing a hat. Shipping the break silently is rejected outright: it converts 'no export step' into 'an export step nobody wrote'.

x-v3-changes.two_spellings: move.blocked_as is the spelling; move.engine.blocked_as is accepted and LOSES where both are present. The reason is not indecision, it is that the two placements answer different questions correctly and only one of them can be the file's shape. By this schema's own stated rule ($defs.moveEngine.min_reach_sub) everything the prover cannot see belongs under `engine`, which argues for the engine spelling; by what the field IS -- a designed gameplay property authored per move, peer to `stance` and read constantly while balancing -- it belongs at move level, which is what x-field-classes.G argues and what was chosen. Accepting both costs six lines in the loader and removes the one failure mode that would have been genuinely bad: a field authored in the other place, validating cleanly, and silently doing nothing. The precedent for tolerating two spellings rather than breaking a file is cancel_families / cancel_rules, which v2 declined to unify on exactly these grounds.
x-v3-changes.the_check_that_was_refused: NOTHING CROSS-CHECKS stance AGAINST blocked_as -- not an error, and deliberately not even a warning -- and that is a decision, recorded here so it is not later mistaken for an omission and 'fixed'. The candidate checks all looked reasonable: warn when a `crouching` move is not `low`; warn when an `air` move is not `high`; warn when a `standing` move is `low`. Every one of them encodes the word USUALLY, and every one of them fires on a move somebody has shipped. A crouching heavy punch is commonly a MID anti-air. A standing overhead is a standing move blocked high. Aerials are stopped by a low block in most games. All fifteen cells of the grid are legal. A load-time diagnostic that fires on correct data is how a check gets deleted -- A04's scope_correction in this very file records an assertion authored from reasoning that rejected all three corpus characters, and CharacterData.cpp's A01 note gives the same warning in the same words. The two fields are ORTHOGONAL; the schema says so, the loader's header says so at length, and neither of them says it with a check that would be wrong.
narrowings: NONE ON ANY FIELD THAT EXISTS. v3 removes no value, no field and no default. Every file that validated against v2 validates against v3, which is the property x-migration exists to protect and the one v2 could not quite claim -- v2 removed `multiplicative` from decay.kind and had to argue that the removal was free.

ONE NARROWING ON TWO KEYS THAT DO NOT: `move.engine.priority` and `move.engine.invincibility` are now declared invalid ($defs.moveEngine, as `not: {}`) and the loader refuses them by name. Strictly this IS a narrowing and it is listed rather than waved through, because moveEngine has no `additionalProperties: false` and both keys were therefore valid-and-ignored under v2. IT COSTS NOTHING, MEASURED: neither key is authored by any of the five character files, and neither could have meant anything if it were, since nothing has ever read them. What it buys is that the one spelling an author is most likely to guess wrong fails loudly instead of validating and doing nothing. See one_spelling_for_the_other_two.
relaxations: move.stance goes from enum [any, ground, air] to [any, ground, air, standing, crouching]. `ground` KEEPS ITS MEANING -- grounded, stance unspecified -- rather than becoming a deprecated alias for `standing`, because that is what a MUGEN import honestly knows and because turning it into an alias would silently re-label ten transcribed moves as standing when six of them are crouching.
engine.schema_version goes from enum [1, 2] to [1, 2, 3], for the identical reason v2 widened it from const 1: without it no v2 file could validate against v3.
x-v3-changes.renames: None. No field is renamed, retyped, or given a new default. In particular `move.guard` is untouched and keeps its meaning as a RESOURCE MINIMUM; the new block-height field is called blocked_as specifically so that it cannot be confused with it, and any future reader tempted to unify the two names should read $defs.move.blocked_as first. AND ONE DELIBERATE REUSE, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE DECISION TO blocked_as AND NEEDS ITS REASON RECORDED. `move.priority` is a new key whose name is already in this schema twice -- engine.projectile.priority and engine.reaction.priority, both MUGEN parameters. blocked_as was RENAMED away from `guard` because the collision was on THE SAME OBJECT, where two ideas would have shared one key; this collision is two nesting levels down, and the [G]-at-move-level / [E]-under-engine relationship is exactly the one blocked_as already has with engine.reaction.attack_type. Repeating an established pattern beats inventing a fourth word for the concept every fighting game calls priority. THE HAZARD IS THEREFORE NOT THE NAME BUT THE SCALE, and it is documented at $defs.move.priority instead of being renamed away: MUGEN's parameter has its default in the middle of a small band, this field's default is 0 and the bottom of its range is far below, so the SAME NUMBER means 'below normal' in one and 'beats everything normal' in the other. No assertion can catch a value that is legal in both.
what_v3_does_not_close: THE ATTACKER'S HALF OF LOW-PROFILING, AND THIS IS THE ONE TO READ FIRST. hurtbox_sub gives the DEFENDER a height. It gives the ATTACK nothing, because this schema still authors NO VERTICAL EXTENT FOR AN ATTACK AT ALL -- move.reach is a single horizontal scalar and MatchBuilder.cpp's loss table states the consequence in as many words: 'The schema authors no vertical extent for an attack at all. Every hitbox therefore spans the whole body height, so a low kick hits a fighter at the top of a jump.' A low profile is two boxes failing to overlap, and v3 types one of them. UNTIL THE OTHER EXISTS, A SHORTER HURTBOX IS DATA NOTHING CONSUMES: the behaviour the author asked for is expressible in the file and not yet computable from it. That is stated here rather than left to be discovered, because the field looks finished and is not. The remedy is deliberately cheap -- $defs.boxSub is named generically and carries no hurtbox semantics, so an attack's box is a `hitbox_sub` referencing the same def, not a second box type to keep in sync. It is not added here because nothing consumes it either, and a schema field with neither data nor a reader behind it is what ADR-001:98-100 tells Phase 3 not to accumulate.

ENFORCEMENT. This is data, not behaviour, and the gap is wide enough to state plainly: MatchBuilder.cpp already reports `move.stance` as a KernelPermits loss over every move in every file, because the kernel gates starting a move on hitstun and blockstun only. Nothing enforces stance today, and v3 makes the field precise without making it enforced -- a `crouching` move remains startable in the air. Blocking is in the same position and further back: cse::kernel::Combat.h scopes blocking out entirely ('Fighter::blockstun exists and nothing ever writes it'), so `blocked_as` has nothing to be checked against yet. Both are Phase 3 kernel work, both will need their own loss-table entries, and authoring the data first is the right order -- the alternative is a kernel rule with no file able to describe the character it applies to.

PER-FRAME HURTBOXES. hurtbox_sub is ONE box for a WHOLE move. A move whose profile genuinely changes shape mid-animation is over-approximated by whatever box it authors, and the honest response is engine.transcription_note rather than authoring the tallest frame and calling it exact. The per-frame track is engine.anim.frames[].hurt, it is still an untyped array, and Phase 3's hitbox editor owns it.

COMMAND NORMALS. The author scoped them out explicitly -- 'on a character by character basis we can also have command normals (direction+punch or kick) - but this can be something for later' -- and v3 adds nothing for them. Worth noting that the missing piece is not a stance or a block height, both of which a command normal already has: it is INPUT NOTATION, which MatchBuilder.h records this schema as lacking altogether. That is a separate hole and naming it here stops the next person looking for it under `stance`.

THE PROVER HALF OF ALL FIVE FIELDS. The prover models one attacker's combo against an abstract defender with no state (x-known-over-approximations.defender_has_no_state), so it has no blocking, no stance, no boxes, no trades and nothing that can be made invulnerable, and no field can give it any. Nothing here is a loss the fragment could have carried and did not. Priority is the clearest case in the group: it is a property of TWO fighters meeting on one tick, and the prover analyses ONE character's cancel graph, so there is no instant in its model at which the field could be consulted even in principle.

REVERSAL BEATS MEATY, AND THIS IS THE HALF OF THE REQUEST THAT CANNOT BE FINISHED YET. The request names two cases: anti-airs beating aerials, and 'certain invincible reversals would have priority over meaty attacks (attacks on knockdown as the player gets up)'. THE FIRST LANDS COMPLETELY -- `aerial` is a token, move.stance already types the attacker as airborne, and nothing else is needed. THE SECOND CANNOT, BECAUSE THERE IS NO KNOCKDOWN STATE AT ALL. Not a missing field: cse::kernel::GameState has no Lying, no wakeup, no getup timer and no concept of a defender on the floor, so a `meaty` is an attack timed against a state that does not exist and there is nothing for a reversal to have priority OVER. The two new fields are not what is missing and neither of them should grow a `meaty` token to paper over it -- the correct sequence is a knockdown state first, and then it needs no new schema field, because an invincible reversal on wakeup is already this pair of fields doing exactly what they do everywhere else. AND THE ROOT OF IT IS ONE ALREADY-RECORDED DEFECT: MUGEN's statetype is S/C/A/**L**, and ADR-006 section 1.3 records that the importer's `("S", "C")` tuple dropped the C -- but the same expression drops the L too, falling through to ANY, which is the permissive direction. move.stance gained `standing` and `crouching` in this revision and did NOT gain a lying value, deliberately: a stance is the state a move STARTS in and nobody starts a move lying down. The knockdown state belongs in GameState, not here.

ENFORCEMENT OF FIELDS 4 AND 5, WHICH IS ADR-005 P2 AND IS BATCHED FOR A STATED REASON. Neither field is read by the kernel today, and the batching is not scheduling convenience: GameState is a wire contract with a golden cross-toolchain hash over it, so every separate change to what the simulation reads pays the re-golden cost again, and P2 already groups blocking, resources, hitstop and pushback for that reason. TWO FACTS THE ENFORCEMENT WORK WILL WANT, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE THEY ARE TRUE NOW AND CHEAP TO LOSE. (a) THE ARCHITECTURE ALREADY ANTICIPATED PRIORITY BY NAME. cse/kernel/Combat.cpp lines 264-290 is three loops -- decide every overlap from the same pre-hit state, then apply effects, then apply interruptions -- and its comment says why: 'whether it got to land its own blow would depend on which slot happened to be checked first ... it is stable, so it never looks like nondeterminism locally and instead just makes player 1 lose trades.' The same comment ends 'Priority and trade resolution proper ... are Phase 3; the rule here is the symmetric one, and both fighters land.' Priority slots into the tail of the DECIDE loop and invincibility into its body; both are pure functions of the pre-hit state, so the property those three loops exist to preserve survives unchanged. (b) THE DEFAULTS ARE THE CURRENT BEHAVIOUR. Priority 0 everywhere means every meeting is a tie means every meeting is a trade, which is what ResolveHits does today; no invincibility window means every overlap lands, which is also what it does today. So the day the kernel starts reading these fields, EVERY EXISTING CHARACTER MUST PLAY IDENTICALLY, and that is a regression test rather than a hope.

x-known-over-approximations.$comment: ADR-001 names three halves that a schema field cannot close, and rule 3 of this work item requires each to be documented as a bounded over-approximation with its DIRECTION stated. ADR-001:224-225 fixes the vocabulary: the permissive direction 'can invent an infinite but cannot hide one' and is safe; the other direction hides infinites and is a soundness bug. TWO OF THE THREE ERR SAFE. ONE DOES NOT, and it is named as a soundness bug below rather than softened.

min_reach.closable_half: The ENGINE half is closed by move.engine.min_reach_sub + input.proximity_variant. The engine knows the threshold and picks the right state.
min_reach.unclosable_half: The PROVER half. move.reach expresses a MAXIMUM gap because model.py:473-476 emits a `__space >= max_reach - reach` guard and __space is max_reach - gap (model.py:495-497). A MINIMUM gap is an upper bound on a resource, and the fragment's only comparison is componentwise >= (comboprover.hpp:256-262). There is no encoding.
min_reach.direction: PERMISSIVE -- SAFE. The model lets the attacker use a far normal point-blank, granting a move the real character would replace with its close variant. It can invent an infinite; it cannot hide one.
min_reach.bound: Confined to the 8 moves in 2 characters that carry a proximity_variant. On Kung Fu Girl the pair is stand_hk_far/stand_hk_close (corpus/kfg/Kung Fu Girl.cmd:802) and the over-credit is at most the difference between the two moves' frame data.
min_reach.partially_closable_after_all: The CLOSER member's constraint IS expressible today and ADR-001 does not say so. stand_hk_close is selected only at gap <= 15 px and `reach` is exactly an upper bound on the gap, so authoring reach 0.15 instead of the 0.52 taken from its Clsn1 box would encode the selector exactly and remain sound. Not done here because reach is [P] and the change must be re-measured; offered to Phase 3.

projectile_contact_frame.closable_half: The ENGINE half is closed by move.engine.projectile: spawn tick, velocity, lifetime and the projectile's own hit profile are all now expressible.
projectile_contact_frame.unclosable_half: The PROVER half. Move.startup is a constant; a fireball's frame of contact is a function of distance. 'Startup 15' means only 'released on frame 15'. VERIFIED against the corpus: Kung Fu Man's hasyo has startup 15, and the Projectile controller fires on animelem=10 of anim 1100 (corpus/kfm/kfma4a_cns.txt:2429), whose first tick is 15 (corpus/kfm/kfma4a.air:1448 and the nine elements before it). The two coincide exactly, which is the point -- startup measures release, not contact.
projectile_contact_frame.direction: CONSERVATIVE -- THIS IS THE DANGEROUS ONE, AND IT IS A SOUNDNESS BUG, NOT A SAFE APPROXIMATION. Reasoning: the prover measures hitstun from the moment the move connects and measures every cancel delay from that same moment. A projectile's authored delay is derived from the attacker's own animation and is therefore measured from RELEASE, while in reality the defender's hitstun begins at CONTACT, which is f ticks later. The model therefore starts and ends the defender's hitstun f ticks too early while the attacker's follow-up availability is unchanged, so the model credits the attacker with LESS frame advantage than reality gives. Less advantage means a loop the real character can perform may be reported dead. That HIDES an infinite, which ADR-001:224-225 and :369-374 both classify as the unacceptable direction -- it is the same failure the rejected `meter_room` design was rejected for.
projectile_contact_frame.bound_and_why_the_phase_0_verdicts_are_u: MEASURED, not argued: hasyo and suiten_hasyo have ZERO outgoing cancels in kung_fu_man.json (8 and 5 incoming, 0 outgoing each). The under-credited advantage is the advantage AFTER a projectile connects, and no edge in any of the three files consumes it. The unsoundness is therefore real, latent, and inert across the entire Phase-0 corpus, and Kung Fu Man's TERMINATING verdict does not rest on it.
projectile_contact_frame.what_would_close_it: Not a schema field. Either a distance-dependent startup in the fragment -- which is a new Move shape, not a new key -- or, cheaply and soundly, authoring a projectile move's outgoing cancel delays as if contact were at the minimum plausible range, which over-credits the attacker and flips the direction to the safe one. Phase 3 must do the second before authoring the first such edge, and this note exists so that it is a decision rather than an accident.

'comboprover has no state for the defender at all.' A predicate language over the defender does not help, because there is no defender for it to be about; this is a property of the fragment, and no v2 field and no Phase 5 grammar closes it.

x-load-assertions.$comment: Rules that JSON Schema draft 2020-12 cannot express, because each compares one part of the document to another or one file to another. They are listed here with ids so the adapter can implement them and cite them, exactly as v1 made the v2 backlog queryable rather than prose. ADR-001 section 8 item 3 explicitly asks for the decay pair to be 'asserted at load'. STATUS: A01-A04 are verified against all three shipped files in x-v2-verification.

A01.why: max(floor, base - step*n) means a floor above a base RAISES it and invents frame advantage (model.py:260, comboprover.hpp:81)

A02.why: repeated float multiply then truncate, reproducible by neither integer kernel

A03.rule: every character in a build declares the same resources in the same order
A03.why: comboprover::Character keys a ResourceVec by INDEX (comboprover.hpp:56, :128-129, :152), so a mismatch silently compares meter against juggle

A04.rule: no MOVE effect/guard map and no CANCEL effect/guard map authors the key `__space`. Gap actions are exempt and MUST be able to author it
A04.why: On a move the prover MERGES rather than honours an authored value -- model.py:476 does guard[SPACE] = max(authored, need) and :479 does effect[SPACE] = authored - units(pushback) -- so an authored number silently combines with a derived one and the file no longer says what it appears to say. On a GAP ACTION the opposite is true: authoring `__space` is the only way to express displacement, and it is the documented mechanism ('walking forward is simply a positive effect on the distance resource', gap.py:54-56). model.py:510 APPENDS a synthesized `walk` action alongside the authored list rather than colliding with it.
A04.scope_correction: An earlier draft of this assertion said 'no effect or guard map' unqualified, and its `why` claimed a collision with model.py:495-497. Both were wrong. Executed as written it rejects all three Phase-0 characters -- kung_fu_girl and kung_fu_man author {__space: 0} on gap_action `microdash`, aof2 authors {__space: 170} on `run_close` -- and two of this schema's own worked examples. It was authored from reasoning and never run against the corpus, which is the same defect class as the `derivation_legend` type error and the A06 over-fire recorded below. Verified before and after: 3 of 3 characters violate the old wording, 0 of 3 violate this one.

A05.why: the [P] scalars must be the first hit, because every cancel delay is measured from first contact

A06.rule: consider only the UNCONDITIONAL hit records, i.e. those with no `condition`. If the last of those has a hitstun_ticks differing from hits[0]'s, then engine.hits_projection_caveat must be present and must name the direction
A06.why: the projection is then an approximation whose direction depends on the numbers, and the conservative direction hides infinites
A06.applies_when: engine.hits has more than one unconditional entry
A06.why_conditional_records_are_excluded: A record carrying a `condition` is an ALTERNATIVE profile, not a sequel -- Kung Fu Girl's chop registers its second HitDef only when the first WHIFFED (corpus/kfg/Normal.cns:224), so the two are mutually exclusive and the second is never 'the last hit of the combo'. An earlier draft of this assertion omitted the exclusion and fired on chop, which is how the distinction was found: it flagged a 30-vs-33 hitstun difference between two hits that can never both land. Counting an alternative as a sequel would also credit the attacker with 198 damage from one button.

A08.rule: motion[].tick strictly increasing, and every velocity an integer
A08.why: ARCHITECTURE.md:47 -- the authoritative core is int32 sub-units

A09.why: for a projectile move, startup means release and nothing else (ADR-001:246-247)

A10.rule: a transition with kind on_land must carry duration_bound and duration_derivation
A10.why: move.recovery is then an approximation and only the author knows its direction; a default would let the infinite-hiding direction ship silently

A11.rule: if any gap action declares a non-null engine.variant, then engine.variants.prover_reading must be present and notes[] must carry the union warning
A11.why: the prover sees the union of all variants, so an INFINITE verdict may name a route no single sub-character can perform

A12.rule: every [P] field has a sibling engine.derivation entry naming a file:line or saying ESTIMATED in capitals
A12.note: v1's stated rule, unchanged; warning rather than error because derivation_defaults legitimately covers most moves

A13.rule: move.engine.min_reach_sub is set only on a move whose engine.input.proximity_variant.selects is this_when_farther
A13.why: they are the same fact written twice; the closer member has a maximum, not a minimum

A14.why: a move cannot take the character off the ground before it starts or after it has ended. The number's whole job is to answer 'is the attacker on the floor on tick N' for the ticks this move occupies; outside them it answers a question about a move that is not running, which is not a smaller claim but an incoherent one.
A14.why_the_upper_bound_is_the_looser_of_two: STATED BECAUSE IT IS AN OFF-BY-ONE THIS ASSERTION DELIBERATELY DECLINES TO ARBITRATE. This schema's tick base is 1-based -- $defs.move: 'tick 1 is the first tick of the state' -- and mugen_cns.py:560-561 derives recovery as `total animation ticks - startup - active + 1`, so under the schema's own arithmetic the last tick of a move is startup + active + recovery - 1. The kernel counts differently: cse::kernel::Combat.h makes the first tick FRAME 0 and MatchBuilder.cpp computes `duration = startup + active + recovery` with the last frame at duration - 1. The two bases differ by one at the end. This bound takes the LOOSER of them, so a file that is correct under either reading passes. That is the deliberate direction: A14 exists to catch NONSENSE -- tick 0, a negative, tick 400 on a twenty-tick move -- and a load assertion that rejects a correct file over a one-frame convention dispute it does not own is the failure mode A04's scope_correction records at length. Tightening it is a job for whoever unifies the two tick bases, and that is a decision with a golden hash under it.
A14.proved_by: MUTATION. Take any fighter_a move that authors engine.airborne_from_tick and set it to 0: refused, because tick 0 is before the move exists. Set it to startup + active + recovery + 1: refused, because the move has ended. Set it to 1 or to exactly startup + active + recovery: accepted, and those two are the boundary the assertion is asserting.

A15.rule: move.engine.hurtbox_sub is a WELL-FORMED, NON-EMPTY box within the kernel's coordinate bound: x0 < x1, y0 < y1, and every coordinate's magnitude <= cse::kernel::kMaxBoxCoord (1 << 20 sub-units, 4096 px)
A15.why: Combat.h::BoxIsValid states this rule for the simulation and says where it belongs -- 'Exposed for the data loader, which is where a bad box should be rejected -- the simulation itself is total and never needs to ask.' Each clause fails differently and each failure is silent. An INVERTED box (x1 < x0) is an inside-out rectangle that every half-open overlap test reports as empty, so the character would simply never be hit and nothing would say why -- Combat.h names this exact trap when it explains why MirrorBox negates AND swaps. An EMPTY box (x0 == x1) is total, permanent, unattributed invulnerability authored as four innocent-looking integers, when the schema already has engine.invuln[] to say which attack classes and for how many ticks. An OUT-OF-BOUND coordinate is worse than either, because it is not rejected downstream: PlaceBox CLAMPS, so the box would silently change shape rather than fail, which MatchBuilder.cpp already refuses for the body and for reach on the same grounds.
A15.how_it_is_checked_without_linking_the_ke: BY WRITING THE RULE OUT, WHICH IS THE ESTABLISHED SHAPE HERE AND NOT A NEW IDEA. Games/UntitledFighter/Data/CMakeLists.txt ends in a FATAL_ERROR if CseData ever acquires CseKernel on its link line, so BoxIsValid -- an ordinary function defined in Combat.cpp -- cannot be called. MatchBuilder.cpp hit this first and solved it by including cse/kernel/Combat.h for the STRUCTS AND THE CONSTEXPR CONSTANTS ONLY and re-deriving the range check as a local `coordInRange`; its own comment calls duplicating four comparisons 'the cheaper half of that trade'. The loader does the same, against the same kMaxBoxCoord, so the bound cannot drift from the kernel's. ONE DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE FROM MatchBuilder: that file does NOT replicate BoxIsValid's emptiness half, because there a zero-width box is how 'this move has no reach' is expressed and is inert rather than invalid. Here the emptiness half IS replicated, because an empty HURTBOX is not the absence of a thing -- it is invulnerability. Same rule, opposite meanings for the degenerate case, and the difference is worth one sentence in each file.
A15.and_one_clause_that_only_warns: A NEGATIVE y0 IS WARNED ABOUT, NEVER REFUSED, and the clause exists because the mistake it catches is already sitting in a shipped file. $defs.boxSub is +Y UP with the floor at 0 -- the orientation cse::kernel::Box uses and MatchBuilder.cpp builds, [-3328, 0, 3328, 15360] for the default body. But engine.constants.default_pushbox_sub in fighter_a.json is [-3328, -15360, 3328, 0], MUGEN's Y-DOWN convention with the head at -60 px. Those are the SAME BODY written two ways, both are well-formed rectangles, both pass every other clause of A15, and the second one places the character sixty pixels underground. An author reaching for a hurtbox override will reach for the pushbox they already have. It is a warning rather than an error because y0 < 0 is only ALMOST certainly wrong: refusing it would be a claim about every character anyone will ever author, and warning is a claim about this one. The message names the convention and the constant, because 'y0 is negative' on its own tells nobody anything.
A15.proved_by: MUTATION. Take a fighter_a move carrying engine.hurtbox_sub and swap x0 with x1: refused as inverted. Set y1 equal to y0: refused as empty, and that is the mutation that matters most, because it is the one that would otherwise SHIP -- an inverted box at least looks wrong to a reader, while an empty one looks like a box. Set x1 to 2000000 (above 1 << 20): refused as out of bounds, and note that this is the case the kernel would have silently CLAMPED rather than caught, which is why the check has to be here. Paste engine.constants.default_pushbox_sub in verbatim: accepted with the Y-DOWN warning, which is the whole point of that clause -- it is the only one of the four mutations that produces a file the loader is willing to ship.

A16.rule: a character SHOULD declare at least six `standing`, six `crouching` and six `air` moves. Falling short is a WARNING naming each shortfall, never a refusal
A16.why: the author's roster standard is 'we should consider every character will have at least the following: six grounded normals (3 punches, 3 kicks), six crouching normals, six aerial attacks'. It is a DESIGN STANDARD, not a format rule, and the difference decides the severity: `at least` is a floor a designer aims at, and a grappler with no aerials, a boss with four buttons, or a half-finished character mid-block-out must still load. A schema that refuses to open an incomplete character is a schema nobody can author a character in.
A16.what_it_actually_counts_and_why_that_is_: IT COUNTS BY STANCE, AND IT CANNOT COUNT NORMALS. The standard is about NORMALS -- three punches and three kicks -- and this schema has no field distinguishing a normal from a special, a super or a command normal, nor any notion of which button a move belongs to ($defs.moveEngine.input carries a free-form command string and MatchBuilder.h records that 'THE SCHEMA HAS NO INPUT NOTATION'). Recovering that from move ids would be reading behaviour out of the spelling of a string, which is precisely the heuristic ARCHITECTURE.md D7 rejects and which this whole finding began with -- `crouch_mk` and `stand_mk` were only ever distinguishable by their names. So the count is over MOVES DECLARING EACH STANCE, which is an UPPER BOUND on the normals: a character can pass this check on six crouching SPECIALS. The direction is stated because it is the honest one -- a character that FAILS is definitely short, a character that PASSES may not be -- and because the alternative was a check that lies in the comfortable direction.
A16.why_ground_counts_toward_nothing: A move declaring `ground` is GROUNDED, UNSPECIFIED, and counting it as standing or as crouching would invent the very datum the transcription lost. It is counted and reported SEPARATELY instead, which turns the warning on a MUGEN import from a nag into the finding: `kung_fu_girl.json` does not lack crouching normals -- it has six, and the file does not say which they are. That sentence is worth more than a number.
A16.a_known_divergence_from_ADR_006_section_: ADR-006 section 8 tabulates this check counting NORMALS -- it notes that Kung Fu Man has '4 aerial: jump_lp/hp/lk/hk; its other three air moves are specials', and that 'air-stance specials do not satisfy an aerial slot'. THE IMPLEMENTED CHECK CANNOT DO THAT, and the reason is the one above: no field in this schema distinguishes a normal from a special, so A16 counts by STANCE and over-counts wherever a special shares one. The two disagree only on the AIR line and only for characters whose aerials are mostly specials -- on Kung Fu Man, ADR-006's hand count warns about two missing aerials and A16 does not, because it sees seven air-stance moves. Everything else agrees, including every crouching and standing line and the whole of fighter_a. THE ADR'S TABLE IS WHAT A HUMAN COUNTS BY EYE AND A16 IS WHAT A LOADER CAN COUNT; the gap between them is exactly the missing field, and closing it means adding a move CATEGORY to the schema rather than making the loader guess. That is a real candidate for v4 and it is not smuggled in here, because a category field wants the same conversation command normals want (ADR-006 section 8) and neither has had it.
A16.why_it_is_not_gated_on_schema_version: TEMPTING AND REFUSED. Suppressing it for files declaring version 1 or 2 would silence it on exactly the three files where the crouching collapse actually happened, which is the opposite of what the check is for. The collapse was silent once already; that is the whole reason this assertion exists.
A16.proved_by: MUTATION, and it fires on real data before any mutation is needed. MEASURED CENSUS over all five character files, standing / crouching / air / ground: fighter_a 0/0/2/16, fighter_a_infinite 0/0/0/18, kung_fu_girl 0/0/1/24, kung_fu_man 0/0/7/17, aof2 0/0/0/10. Every file warns, and NOT ALL OF THEM WARN THE SAME WAY -- Kung Fu Man's 7 aerials clear the air line and it is warned only about standing and crouching, which is the evidence that the check discriminates rather than firing uniformly on everything. To watch it fall silent on fighter_a instead, re-declare its six stand_* normals as `standing` and its six crouch_* as `crouching`, then add four more `air` moves to the two it has. That list is the shortest complete description of what fighter_a is missing, which is what a warning is for.

A17.why: THE RANGE IS THE TYPE AND THE TYPE IS NOT A FREE CHOICE. This field ends in cse::kernel::MoveDef, whose loaded arrays the connect handshake hashes, and MoveDef carries an explicit 16-bit `pad_` placed there because 'hashing a struct with indeterminate padding compares two machines' uninitialised bytes'. A 16-bit signed priority is exactly the slot that already exists. WHAT THE ASSERTION ACTUALLY PREVENTS IS A SILENT TRUNCATION, and the failure is not a clamp -- it is a SIGN FLIP AT THE BOUNDARY: 32768 narrowed to 16 bits is -32768, so the strongest move in the file becomes the weakest, quietly, and only in the build that narrows. A loader that clamped would be worse still, because two peers whose loaders clamped differently would disagree about a hashed byte and the desync would present as a rollback bug rather than as a data error.
A17.what_it_cannot_catch_and_the_reason_that: A NUMBER THAT IS LEGAL AND WRONG. MUGEN's HitDef priority is transcribed at engine.reaction.priority on a different scale with its default in the middle of its band, so a value copied across from there is in range, passes A17, and means the opposite of what it meant. There is no assertion that can tell the two apart -- both are integers and both are legal -- which is why $defs.move.priority spends a paragraph on the scale rather than relying on a check.
A17.proved_by: MUTATION. Author `priority: 40000` on any fighter_a move: refused, naming the bound and the sign flip. `priority: 32767` and `priority: -32768`: accepted, and they are the boundary the assertion is asserting. `priority: 3.5` is also refused, but NOT as A17 -- it fails the ordinary integer check with no rule id, which is the same distinction A02 draws between a banned decay kind and a misspelled one.

A18.rule: every window of move.invincibility[] satisfies from_tick >= 1 and ticks >= 1 and from_tick + ticks - 1 <= move.startup + move.active + move.recovery
A18.why: A window outside the move it belongs to is not a smaller claim, it is an incoherent one: the field answers 'can this move be hit on tick N' for the ticks the move occupies, and outside them it is answering about a move that is not running. ZERO TICKS IS REFUSED BY THE SAME ASSERTION AND FOR A15's REASON ONE FIELD OVER: a window of no length is not a short window, it is the empty set, and it sits in the file looking like protection while providing none. A15 refuses a zero-AREA hurtbox because an empty body is invulnerability that nothing attributes; this refuses a zero-LENGTH window because it is invulnerability that nothing provides. Degenerate geometry and degenerate time fail the same way -- silently, and in the direction that looks correct in a diff.
A18.the_upper_bound_is_A14's_bound_and_delib: A14 already had to choose between two tick bases that disagree by one at the end of a move -- this schema counts from 1 and derives the last tick as startup + active + recovery - 1, while the kernel counts from 0 and MatchBuilder.cpp computes duration = startup + active + recovery -- and it took the LOOSER, so that a file correct under either reading passes. A18 takes the identical bound, computed the identical way, and the reason is not laziness: two assertions on adjacent fields disagreeing by one frame about where a move ENDS would be a worse defect than either bound being loose. Whoever unifies the two tick bases tightens both together, and that is a change with a golden hash under it.
A18.scope_check_before_the_rule_was_written: THIS RULE APPLIES TO move.invincibility[] ONLY AND NOT TO move.engine.invuln[], AND THE SCOPE WAS CHECKED BEFORE THE RULE WAS WRITTEN RATHER THAN AFTER -- which is the whole content of A04's scope_correction. engine.invuln[] is a v2 field with the same from_tick/ticks shape and it is ALREADY AUTHORED IN SHIPPED FILES, so a rule written carelessly over both could have rejected data that works. MEASURED, all five character files: five invuln windows exist, all in the two Editor characters, none in the three MUGEN fixtures -- fighter_a special_uppercut 1..6 against a move ending at 40 and super_beam 1..10 against 54; fighter_a_infinite special_uppercut_l 1..8 against 41, special_uppercut_h 1..10 against 48 and super_beam 1..9 against 57. ZERO OF FIVE fall outside their move. So the rule would have been safe to extend, and it is still not extended, because engine.invuln[] is not loaded at all (CharacterData.h lists it by name among the fields deliberately unread) and an assertion over data nobody parses is an assertion nobody runs. THE MEASUREMENT IS RECORDED ANYWAY, because the day Phase 3 loads engine.invuln[] the question will be asked again, and the answer is already here: extending A18 to cover it costs nothing on any file that exists.
A18.proved_by: MUTATION, against fighter_a's `special_uppercut`, whose startup 3 + active 8 + recovery 29 puts its last tick at 40. Author `invincibility: [{from_tick: 1, ticks: 41}]`: refused, because the window outlives the move by one tick. `{from_tick: 0, ticks: 6}`: refused, because tick 0 is before the move exists. `{from_tick: 41, ticks: 1}`: refused, one tick past the end. `{from_tick: 1, ticks: 6}`: accepted, and it is the migration of that move's own label. `{from_tick: 1, ticks: 40}`: accepted, and it is the exact upper boundary. `{from_tick: 5, ticks: 0}`: refused as degenerate, and that is the mutation that matters most, because a zero-length window is the one a reader's eye slides over.

A19.rule: every entry of move.invincibility[].attack_kinds is one of high, mid, low, aerial, throw, projectile. An unrecognised token is REFUSED, never dropped
A19.why: THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ASSERTION IN THE v3 GROUP, because of which way a typo fails. The kind list NARROWS a window, and an empty list means EVERY kind, so a mistyped token has two ways to go and both are silent and catastrophic in opposite directions. Dropped from the list, `["aerail"]` becomes `[]`, which means invincible to EVERYTHING -- the move silently becomes the strongest in the game. Kept as an unknown kind, it means invincible to something no attack ever is -- the move silently becomes invincible to NOTHING while the file still says `invincible` and the designer still believes it. There is no benign reading. Compare A02's reasoning: an unknown decay kind is refused too, but the value there is a name in a closed set with no arithmetic behind it, while here the same typo changes what the character IS in a way playtesting attributes to balance rather than to a misspelling.
A19.the_reserved_tokens_are_legal_and_are_no: `throw` and `projectile` ARE recognised tokens and are accepted today, even though the kernel can produce neither -- it has no throw at all, and while engine.projectile is real authored data on four moves, nothing in cse::kernel spawns one. A window naming only reserved tokens is INERT and nothing warns about it, because a warning there would fire on correct forward-looking data, which is the failure A04 was corrected for and the failure x-v3-changes.the_check_that_was_refused declined to repeat. Reserving them now costs one enum entry each; adding them later costs a bit position in a mask that by then is inside a hashed struct.
A19.proved_by: MUTATION. On fighter_a's `special_uppercut`, author `attack_kinds: ["aerials"]` -- the plural, which is the typo an author actually makes: refused, naming the token and listing all six legal ones. Author `["air"]`, which is the value move.stance uses for the same idea: also refused, and that is the second mutation worth running, because it is not a typo at all -- it is a reasonable guess from a neighbouring field, and it proves the message has to name the legal set rather than just say `unknown`. Author `["throw"]`: accepted and inert. Author `["high", "mid", "low", "aerial"]`: accepted, and it is the correct migration of `special_uppercut`'s existing engine.invuln source string, which records in prose that throws are deliberately excluded.

A20.rule: move.invincibility: [] is accepted, means exactly what an absent field means -- this move has no invincibility -- and WARNS
A20.why: THE QUESTION IS WHETHER AN EMPTY LIST AND AN ABSENT FIELD MEAN DIFFERENT THINGS, AND HERE THE ANSWER IS NO, WHICH HAS TO BE ARGUED RATHER THAN ASSUMED because this schema has a strong habit of the empty array being load-bearing -- engine.cancel_window_ticks: [] is how the AOF2 thug says it has no cancel window, and ADR-001:541-545 records that a schema which cannot say `none` forces an author to invent a value. THE DIFFERENCE IS THAT `none` IS ALREADY SAYABLE HERE BY SAYING NOTHING, and no default has to be invented for a missing field: a move with no invincibility is the overwhelming majority and is what every character ever authored is. So there is no second meaning left for [] to carry. THE WARNING EXISTS BECAUSE THERE IS EXACTLY ONE OTHER READING AND IT IS THE DANGEROUS ONE. One level down, an absent or empty attack_kinds means EVERY KIND -- full invincibility -- and an author who has just read that rule can reasonably write `invincibility: []` meaning `invincible to everything, always`. That file would load, would say `invincible` to a reader, and would produce a move with no invincibility at all. The warning names both readings and says which one the file got.
A20.why_not_an_error: Because an empty array is not wrong, only uninformative, and a tool that emits the key uniformly for every move must keep working -- refusing it would make this schema harder to generate into than to hand-write, which is backwards. It is the A16 severity argument in miniature: `at least` and `none` are things a file is allowed to say.
A20.and_the_inner_list_is_the_opposite_and_d: attack_kinds ABSENT and attack_kinds [] both mean EVERY KIND, deliberately, and nothing warns about either. The asymmetry with the outer list is not an inconsistency, it is what the two lists DO: the outer list ENUMERATES windows, so having none of them is having no invincibility; the inner list NARROWS one window, so naming nothing is narrowing by nothing, and the identity element of a narrowing is everything. Stating it this way is what makes it memorable enough not to be re-derived wrongly later.
A20.proved_by: MUTATION, and it never fires on any file that ships because no file authors the key. Add `"invincibility": []` to any fighter_a move: the file loads, the move has no invincibility, and the warning says so and names the `invincible to everything` reading it is NOT. Add `"invincibility": [{"from_tick": 1, "ticks": 6}]` -- the same field with the inner list omitted: silent, and the move is invincible to all six kinds for six ticks, which is the reading the warning above tells the author how to reach.
