An INFINITE verdict over it would NOT imply an infinite for any single sub-character, because the search may mix one variant's move with another variant's gap action. Permissive in ADR-001:224-225's sense -- it can invent an infinite, it cannot hide one.

stance_and_blocked_as_are_orthogonal.source_of_the_design: The author's specification, not a corpus line: 'high block covers mid and high attacks, low block covers mid and crouching attacks.'
stance_and_blocked_as_are_orthogonal.moves: fighter_a.json / crouch_mk, crouch_hp, stand_hk -- three moves the file already ships, all three currently declaring `ground` and none of them declaring a block height, because neither field could say anything better when they were written.
stance_and_blocked_as_are_orthogonal.derivation: None: these are the two fields being authored, and the point of the example is the SHAPE of the pair rather than any number. crouch_mk is a sweep-adjacent poke -- crouching, and a low. crouch_hp is an anti-air -- crouching, and a MID, because a move that hits an opponent above you is not something a crouching block is the answer to. stand_hk is standing and mid, like almost everything. The three together are the counterexample that makes the two fields independent.
stance_and_blocked_as_are_orthogonal.note: THIS IS THE EXAMPLE THAT EXISTS TO BE READ BEFORE ANYBODY TRIES TO DELETE A FIELD. crouch_hp is the whole argument in one move: it is `crouching` and it is `mid`. Derive blocked_as from stance and it becomes a low, and a character's anti-air is suddenly beaten by a crouching block, which is a balance change delivered by a refactor. The grid has fifteen legal cells and nothing in this schema cross-checks them -- see x-v3-changes.the_check_that_was_refused for the three checks that were drafted and thrown away, each because it fires on a move somebody has shipped.

low_profile_is_a_shape.source_of_the_design: The author's constraint, quoted because it is what rules out the obvious implementation: 'crouching attacks can low profile high attacks by attack basis (the hurtbox shape for the crouching attack would determine this - not every crouching attack would low profile).'
low_profile_is_a_shape.moves: fighter_a.json / crouch_mk (startup 7, active 4, recovery 16 -- shipped values) and crouch_hp (startup 8, active 4, recovery 22 -- shipped values)
low_profile_is_a_shape.derivation: The standing body comes from fighter_a's own engine.constants: height_px 60 and default_pushbox_sub [-3328, -15360, 3328, 0], i.e. a half-width of 3328 sub-units (13 px). REWRITTEN INTO THIS SCHEMA'S +Y-UP CONVENTION that body is [-3328, 0, 3328, 15360], which is exactly the box MatchBuilder.cpp builds from kDefaultBodyHalfWidthSub and kDefaultBodyHeightSub -- and the sign flip is the trap $defs.boxSub and A15 both warn about. From there the two crouching boxes are CHOSEN, not derived, because no source says how tall this character crouches: crouch_mk presents 26 px (6656) and leans 17 px (4352) forward into the kick; crouch_hp presents 36 px (9216), an ordinary crouch, because it is punching upward and its body stays up with it.
low_profile_is_a_shape.note: THE BEHAVIOUR IS NOT IN EITHER FILE. Nothing anywhere says `crouch_mk low profiles`. It falls out: 6656 is below whatever height a high attack's box starts at, and 9216 may not be. Change the number and the behaviour changes with it, with no flag to remember to update -- which is the entire argument for geometry over a boolean, and it is checkable in a hitbox viewer rather than assertable in prose.
low_profile_is_a_shape.note_on_what_this_example_CANNOT_show: AND IT IS THE IMPORTANT HALF. There is no attack box to compare these bodies against, because THIS SCHEMA STILL AUTHORS NO VERTICAL EXTENT FOR AN ATTACK -- MatchBuilder.cpp says so in its loss table in as many words: 'The schema authors no vertical extent for an attack at all. Every hitbox therefore spans the whole body height, so a low kick hits a fighter at the top of a jump.' v3 closes the DEFENDER's half of low-profiling and not the attacker's. Until an attack has a y-range, a shorter hurtbox is data that nothing consumes, and the interaction below is what WILL happen rather than what does. That hole is named in x-v3-changes.what_v3_does_not_close and $defs.boxSub is deliberately general so that closing it is a reference rather than a second box type.

hurtbox_sub.source: CHOSEN. 26 px tall, 17 px of forward lean. Low-profiles anything whose box begins above 26 px.
CHOSEN. 36 px, an ordinary crouch. Does NOT low-profile a high attack that begins at 28 px, which is the author's 'not every crouching attack would low profile' made arithmetic.

hop_over_is_a_tick.source_of_the_design: The author again: 'grounded attacks that make you airborne can also hop over crouching attacks (ryu's f+HK hop kick being an example for this).'
hop_over_is_a_tick.moves: A DESIGNED MOVE THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET. fighter_a has no hop kick -- its 18 moves are 12 grounded normals, 2 aerials, 3 specials and a super -- so unlike every other example in this object there is nothing to cite. The frame numbers below are CHOSEN and are marked as such; what is being demonstrated is the shape and the assertion boundary, not a transcription.
hop_over_is_a_tick.derivation: A hop kick that leaves the ground on tick 5 of a 41-tick move: startup 20, active 3, recovery 18. A14's bound is 1 <= t <= startup + active + recovery = 41, so tick 5 is comfortably inside it and the move is airborne for the whole of its active window -- which is the point, since an attack that lands before it leaves the floor hops over nothing. Note that 5 is BELOW startup: the character is airborne twelve ticks before the hitbox appears, which is what a hop kick actually does and why the field is not derived from `active`.
hop_over_is_a_tick.note: THE INTERACTION IS SYMMETRIC AND NEITHER MOVE NAMES THE OTHER. crouch_mk above is `low` and presents a 26 px body; this move is off the floor from tick 5. Whether it clears a particular sweep is a question about two boxes and a tick, answerable for every pair in the cast at once. A `hops_over_lows: true` flag on this move would have been wrong the first time two characters' sweeps had different heights, and a `can_be_hopped: true` flag on the sweep would have been wrong the first time two hops had different altitudes.
hop_over_is_a_tick.note_on_the_three_fields_that_overlap: This move needs NONE of transitions[], motion[] or motion_physics to say what it says, and that is deliberate. Kung Fu Girl's knee carries all three because it was transcribed from a state that authors velocities; a designed hop kick has a tick and a box and nothing else, and requiring a physics block to declare one tick is how a field goes unauthored. Where a move does carry more than one of them they must agree, and nothing checks that they do -- there is no data behind such a check yet, and an assertion nobody has watched fire is not an assertion.

hurtbox_sub.source: CHOSEN. The whole body lifted 14 px off the floor -- y0 is 3584, not 0 -- which is what being airborne looks like as geometry and is the one legitimate reason for a non-zero y0.

engine.derivation: CHOSEN THROUGHOUT. This move is not in any character file; it exists to show the field's shape and A14's boundary.

escape_hatch.reason: startup, active, recovery, hitstun, damage, effect and guard are all ordinary; everything v3 adds is engine-only.

the_label_that_became_a_field.moves: fighter_a `special_uppercut`, and unlike the three examples above this one is a MIGRATION of data that is already in the shipped file -- twice, in two places, only one of which a program can read.
the_label_that_became_a_field.what_the_file_says_today: The label is `Uppercut (reversal, invincible 1-6)` and engine.derivation says `3f reversal with 6 ticks of strike invincibility (engine.invuln)`. engine.invuln[0] is from_tick 1, ticks 6, kind not_hit_by, attrs [NA, NP, SA, SP, HA, HP], with a source string reading `Strike invincible for the 3 startup ticks and the first 3 active ticks; throws (NT/ST/HT) are deliberately NOT in the list.`
the_label_that_became_a_field.the_three_problems_with_that_and_the_ord: (1) NOTHING LOADS engine.invuln. CharacterData.h names it among the fields deliberately not read, so the only copy of `1-6` any program can reach is the English one inside the label -- which is the defect MatchBuilder.h already named for buttons and ADR-006 named for stance, arriving a third time. (2) The two copies must be kept in sync BY HAND and agree today only because nobody has edited either; that is D8's failure mode. (3) The MUGEN vocabulary cannot say half of what this move needs even in principle: `NA/SA/HA` classify an attack as normal/special/hyper, and there is no way in it to say `invincible to lows` or `invincible to aerials-as-this-schema-defines-them`.
the_label_that_became_a_field.the_migration: attack_kinds [high, mid, low, aerial] is exactly `strikes and not throws`, and it says so in tokens rather than in a source string: all three guard heights plus airborne attackers, with `throw` deliberately absent. Note that this is NOT the same as an empty list -- an empty list would mean throw-invincible too, which is a different and stronger move. THAT DISTINCTION IS THE POINT: the file has always drawn it, in prose, and this is the first form of it a kernel can read.
the_label_that_became_a_field.note: This example is written here and NOT into fighter_a.json, which was owned by another process while this pass ran. Authoring it is a data job and a small one; the numbers are above and they are the file's own.

invincibility.source: MIGRATED from the label `Uppercut (reversal, invincible 1-6)` and from engine.invuln[0], which say the same thing in English and in MUGEN's letters. Strikes only: throws are excluded and that exclusion is deliberate, which is why `throw` is not in the list and the list is not empty.

a_second_window_would_look_like_this.$comment: NOT authored on this move and shown only for shape -- fighter_a has no throws to be invincible to. It is the request's own example: `a reversal invincible 1-6 and then throw-invincible through its recovery`. The two windows OVERLAP on ticks 1-6 and that is legal and unambiguous; see x-v3-changes.overlap_is_a_union.

anti_air_is_invincibility_and_not_a_prio.source_of_the_design: The author: 'to ensure anti airs properly work we should also probably consider the arc sys works style of priority over aerial attacks ... moves specifically toggled as anti airs - will have priority over aerials.'
anti_air_is_invincibility_and_not_a_prio.moves: fighter_a `crouch_hp`, whose label already reads `Crouching Heavy Punch (anti-air launcher)` -- so the character has had an anti-air all along and no field said so. startup 8, active 4, recovery 22; stance crouching, blocked_as mid.
anti_air_is_invincibility_and_not_a_prio.derivation: One window: from_tick 1, ticks 8, attack_kinds [aerial]. The 8 is `startup`, so the invincibility ends on the tick the hitbox appears -- the move is untouchable by an aerial while it is winding up and ordinary once it is committed, which is what an anti-air is and why the number is not chosen but read off the move. NO `priority` FIELD IS AUTHORED ON IT AT ALL, and that is the demonstration: the request asked for a priority toggled by attack state, and the anti-air behaviour falls out of the general mechanism with the priority field left at its default.
anti_air_is_invincibility_and_not_a_prio.why_the_token_is_only_aerial: Because `[aerial]` alone is what makes it an ANTI-AIR rather than a reversal. fighter_a's air_mp is stance air and blocked_as high; air_hk is air and high. An incoming jumping attack therefore carries BOTH `aerial` and `high`, the window matches on ANY shared token, and it stops. A grounded stand_lp carries `mid` only, shares nothing with the window, and beats crouch_hp clean on frames 1-8 -- which is the balance property that makes the move an anti-air and not simply a good button.
anti_air_is_invincibility_and_not_a_prio.and_what_it_costs: `[aerial]` also stops an aerial LOW, if a character ever has one, because the match is an intersection over a token list rather than a conjunction over two axes. That limit is stated at $defs.invincibilityWindow.attack_kinds and is the price of a closed enum instead of a predicate language.

invincibility.source: DESIGNED. Airborne attackers cannot touch it for the whole of its 8-frame startup, ending on the first active tick. Grounded attacks are unaffected, which is what stops an anti-air from being a universally winning button.

priority_is_for_what_invincibility_canno.moves: fighter_a `super_beam` (startup 8, active 2, recovery 44) against any of its twelve grounded normals.
priority_is_for_what_invincibility_canno.derivation: CHOSEN, and the value is the only thing here that is: 10 on the super, nothing authored anywhere else so every other move is 0. On the one tick where the beam and a jab would both connect, 10 > 0, the beam lands and THE JAB DEALS NOTHING. Today, and for every character in the repository, the same tick produces a trade and both land.
priority_is_for_what_invincibility_canno.why_this_case_needs_priority_and_the_ant: A super that beats a jab is not invulnerable to it -- the beam can be hit perfectly well on any other frame, by that same jab, and making it invincible for 54 ticks would be a wildly stronger move and a different design. What is wanted is an ORDERING ON ONE INSTANT, and that is all this field is. The pair divides cleanly: invincibility says `cannot be touched`, priority says `wins the exchange`, and the two together cover the request without either of them growing a condition.
priority_is_for_what_invincibility_canno.the_default_is_the_argument: Note that this example is the ONLY thing in it that changes behaviour. Twelve normals, two aerials, three specials: none authors `priority`, all compare 0 against 0, every meeting between them stays the trade ResolveHits already produces. A field whose default reproduces the shipped game exactly is a field that can land as data long before a kernel reads it, which is why it is in this revision and its enforcement is in ADR-005 P2.

a_move_that_should_lose.$comment: Shown because it is the reason the type is SIGNED. A move that trades badly on purpose -- a committal heavy, a taunt -- is -1, which requires renumbering nothing. With an unsigned type the only way to express `below everything` is to raise every other move in the cast, which is a data migration bought for one bit.

x-v2-where-floats-remain.$comment: ARCHITECTURE.md:47 (D2) requires integers for everything the simulation integrates over time, and ADR-001:311-315 records that D2 'survives, strengthened' because no move needed a float to say what it does. v2 ADDS NO FLOATS. Every field v2 introduces is an integer, in sub-units where it is a distance or a velocity, in hundredths where it is damage, in permille where it is a ratio. The floats below are all inherited from v1 and each has a reason to stay.
x-v2-where-floats-remain.damage: float in both implementations (json_spec.py:69, and Move.damage in model.py). Feeds Result.maxDamage only and never the verdict. The engine's integer original is engine.quantized_sources.damage_hundredths and, per hit, engine.hits[].damage_hundredths.
x-v2-where-floats-remain.reach: float reach units, quantized by the prover itself at model.py:465-468 to hundredths. The engine's integer original is quantized_sources.reach_px; the simulation never reads the float.
x-v2-where-floats-remain.pushback: same as reach, and it is an ESTIMATE regardless of its type (ADR-001:486-494) -- making it an integer would not make it derived.
x-v2-where-floats-remain.walk_speed: float reach units per frame, quantized at model.py:468. ADR-001:499-504 documents the one place this rounds: Kung Fu Man's 2.4 px/tick is 614 sub-units exactly for the engine but lands on 2 px/tick for the prover, losing 0.4. UNDER-states attacker mobility, so it can hide an infinite but not invent one.
x-v2-where-floats-remain.scaling_and_decay_table: float multiplier arrays. Integer permille originals live in quantized_sources.scaling_permille and decay_table_permille. decay.ratio is now dead (see x-v2-changes.narrowings).
x-v2-where-floats-remain.why_they_are_not_converted: Every one of them is a [P] field. Retyping a [P] field would break json_spec.py's float() coercions or change a verdict, and v2's contract is that it changes neither. The integer originals sit beside them in engine.quantized_sources, which is what makes D8 checkable -- ADR-001 section 8 leaves the [P] surface alone deliberately.

x-v3-verification.the_negative_controls: VERIFIED, because a schema that accepts everything is not a schema. Six mutations were each confirmed to be REFUSED: stance `ducking`, blocked_as `overhead`, airborne_from_tick 0 (below the minimum of 1), a hurtbox_sub missing y1, a hurtbox_sub carrying an extra key (additionalProperties false), and schema_version 4. Note what the FIRST of those means in practice -- widening an enum does not weaken it, and a typo in a stance is still caught. TEN MORE FOR FIELDS 4 AND 5, each confirmed REFUSED: attack_kinds `["aerials"]` (the plural, which is the typo an author makes); attack_kinds `["air"]` (which is not a typo at all -- it is move.stance's word for the same idea, guessed from the neighbouring field, and it is the mutation that justifies the error message listing all six legal tokens rather than saying `unknown`); ticks 0; from_tick 0; a window spelling the list `kinds` instead of `attack_kinds` (caught by additionalProperties false, which is why the window def has it); a window missing `ticks`; priority 40000; priority 3.5; `engine.priority`; and `engine.invincibility` -- the last two by the `not: {}` declarations added to $defs.moveEngine, so the schema and the loader refuse the same two misplacements for the same reason. SIX MORE CONFIRMED ACCEPTED, because a negative control alone proves only that a schema refuses things: `invincibility: []`, attack_kinds omitted, attack_kinds `[]`, attack_kinds `["throw"]`, priority at both boundaries 32767 and -32768, and two overlapping windows on one move.
x-v3-verification.the_new_assertions_do_not_reject_anythin: VERIFIED by running A14's, A15's, A17's, A18's, A19's and A20's rules over all five character files: ZERO errors and ZERO warnings from the six of them, because no existing file authors any of the fields they govern. FOR A18 THAT ANSWER IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS AND THE STRONGER ONE WAS TAKEN: engine.invuln[] has the same window shape and IS authored, five times, so A18's rule was additionally run against those five windows even though A18's scope excludes them -- all five sit inside their move, so the rule would have been safe there too. That is recorded at A18.scope_check_before_the_rule_was_written, and running a new rule against the nearest EXISTING data rather than only against the empty field it governs is the discipline A04 was corrected for lacking. That is the expected answer and it is worth having rather than assuming, since the cost of being wrong is five characters that stop loading. A16 is a warning and fires on all five, which is the design -- and it does NOT fire identically on all five, which is the part that matters: Kung Fu Man's 7 aerials clear the air line, so it is warned about standing and crouching only. A check that fired the same way on everything would be measuring nothing. Full census in x-load-assertions.A16.proved_by.
x-v3-verification.what_json_schema_cannot_check_and_the_lo: A14's upper bound compares airborne_from_tick against three sibling fields; A15's emptiness and inversion clauses compare a box's own coordinates against each other and against a kernel constant; A16 counts across the whole moves array; A18 compares a window's own two numbers against three sibling fields of its grandparent move. None of the four is expressible in draft 2020-12, which is why x-load-assertions exists and why all four are implemented in Games/UntitledFighter/Data/src/CharacterData.cpp rather than here. The JSON Schema half catches shape; the loader half catches sense. THREE OF THE v3 ASSERTIONS ARE THE OTHER WAY ROUND AND ARE STATED IN BOTH PLACES ON PURPOSE: A17's range is `minimum`/`maximum` on move.priority, A19's token set is an `enum` on attack_kinds, and A20's empty array is expressible as nothing at all. JSON Schema can catch all three -- and the loader checks them anyway, because NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY VALIDATES A CHARACTER AGAINST THIS DOCUMENT AT RUNTIME. Validation is a thing a person runs; the loader is the thing a match runs. A rule that exists only here is a rule that protects a review and not a build.

what_v2_does_not_close: ADR-001 section 4 group H -- 'the transition is a policy, not a rule'. AOF2 selects its attack with random < 50 evaluated every tick (corpus/aof2/States.st:189, :196). ADR-001:281-284 says D7's escape hatch does not cover this and recommends that AI selection be a SEPARATE AUTHORED ARTIFACT, not a field in this file. v2 agrees: the probability appears only as predicateList.unmodelled prose, and the artifact is ADR-001 section 8 item 5's to design.

ADR-001 section 4 group I's other two shapes. Kung Fu Man's var(3) adds and removes whole MOVES and its var(5) doubles every special into light/strong (ADR-001:295-298). engine.variants can index them, but a mode variable that changes the move LIST is a Phase 3 runtime question about which automaton is loaded, not a schema field.

The one irreducible C++ effect. Kung Fu Man's fuyo_reikyaku sets air.velocity = -vel x, vel y-1.35-pos y/686.68 (corpus/kfm/kfma4a_cns.txt:4060-4070) -- arithmetic over the defender's live position and velocity at the instant of contact. ADR-001:84-89 confirms the prover's verdict is untouched by it because startup, active, recovery, hitstun, damage, effect and guard are all ordinary; it is the engine's hit resolver that cannot be data here. This is the 1 of 59 that D7's escape hatch exists for.
The pushback estimate, which is not a schema problem and is the number every midscreen verdict turns on (ADR-001:386-404, :508-510).
